title: Unshared files and folders are displayed as "Shared"
body: I configured Authentik as a SAML provider and Nextcloud user_saml to use it. In Nextcloud 28.0.3 on an Ubuntu 22.04 Nextcloud AIO Docker deployment, files and folders owned by the Authentik-created user are shown as "Shared by <logged in user>" even though they have not been shared. A user created directly in Nextcloud and signed in through the direct login does not show that label. Authentication itself works normally.

symptoms_visible: My unshared files and folders are labelled "Shared by" me when I sign in with the account created through Authentik and user_saml.
A user created directly in Nextcloud does not get the incorrect shared label.
N0.label: N0 incorrect shared label reported

symptoms_visible: I can also see the incorrect shared status on a local development instance using only local users.
N1.label: N1 non-SAML reproduction established

symptoms_visible: Files are incorrectly shown as shared when the owner's UID consists only of numbers.
I see the same result with local and LDAP users and with both local login and SSO; accounts whose UIDs are not purely numeric do not show it.
N2.label: N2 numeric UID condition isolated

symptoms_visible: On my currently installed affected build, files owned by a purely numeric UID are still displayed as shared.
N3.label: N3 server owner-rendering bug diagnosed

symptoms_visible: After updating my AIO instance, files belonging to my purely numeric username are no longer displayed as shared.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix reported by another affected operator

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced with a local user on an instance that does not use Authentik or user_saml?
Do affected accounts have to come from the SAML backend?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I saw the same incorrect shared status today on my local development instance running the latest code, and all of its users were local users.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can reproduce it only with Authentik-provisioned users; every local user on the same instance displays ownership correctly.
I reproduced it with a local user on a separate Docker development instance rather than the latest master checkout.

edges.comment: Messages c19-c21: maintainer nickvergessen observed the same UI symptom on a local development instance and confirmed that all users there were local. This affected maintainer is folded into the simulated user side; the evidence rules out a SAML-only causal chain.

question_patterns: What account property differs consistently between users that show the label and users that do not?
Does the problem correlate with the format of the user's UID?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After multiple tests, I found that it happens when the user's UID contains only numbers. It does not happen for my users whose UIDs are not purely numeric.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The affected and unaffected users have the same UID format; only users provisioned through Authentik show the label.
It happens with both short and long numeric UIDs, while alphabetical and mixed UIDs remain unaffected.

question_patterns: Does changing the user source or login method affect the result?
Can you compare local and directory users using local login and SSO?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried local users and LDAP users, as well as local login and identity-provider SSO. The source and login method did not matter; the issue followed the purely numeric UID.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: LDAP and local users are unaffected even with numeric UIDs; it occurs only for user_saml accounts.

question_patterns: Which Nextcloud major versions show the behavior?
Did you compare the same account setup across older versions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I observed it in major versions 28 and 29, but not in version 27.

edges.comment: Message c23: affected user participant4 volunteered a multi-version and multi-backend test matrix. That affected user's observations are folded into the simulated user side without attributing the original reporter's SAML configuration to this separate deployment.

solution.intent: Treat the symptom as a Nextcloud server file-list owner parsing and rendering bug triggered by purely numeric UIDs, and correct the owner handling so owned files are not rendered as shared.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainer identified an issue parsing owners and rendering the shared status and reported that the correction was included in recent or upcoming patch releases for the affected major branches.
solution.inference_hint: The affected users supplied the reproduction matrix: numeric UIDs trigger the symptom regardless of local, LDAP, or SAML origin. The maintainer supplied the accepted diagnosis that owner parsing and shared-status rendering were faulty; users did not derive that implementation-level conclusion themselves.

edges.comment: Messages c23-c28: participant4 isolated the numeric-UID condition, while skjnldsv identified an owner-parsing/shared-status rendering issue and stated that it had been fixed for the affected release branches. Release scheduling details are deliberately not scored.

solution.intent: Update to a build containing the owner parsing and shared-status rendering correction, then verify with the same numeric-UID account before declaring the deployment resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Install the appropriate patched maintenance release and revisit the Files view with the affected numeric-UID account. One AIO operator reported the issue solved after updating to 29.0.4, but later operators reported superficially similar cases, so each deployment still needs its own retest.

edges.comment: Message c31: affected participant participant2 confirmed the numeric-username case was solved after updating an AIO deployment. This is terminal-side verification by a different operator, not a retest by original reporter reporter. Messages c32-c38 contain later reports that may represent a different or regressed case; the maintainer requested a separate issue, so they are not spliced into the opening reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a Nextcloud server owner-parsing/shared-status rendering bug triggered by purely numeric user UIDs, rather than an Authentik or user_saml authentication defect.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the cross-backend evidence: local, LDAP, and SAML users can be affected, while the behavior follows UID format and was observed in versions 28 and 29 but not 27.
Must not recommend reconfiguring Authentik attributes or replacing user_saml as the primary fix, because the same symptom was reproduced with local users and independently of the login method.
Must recommend using a build containing the owner-rendering correction and ask the affected operator to retest the numeric-UID account before declaring that deployment resolved.

Must not claim that the original reporter verified the fix: the thread only contains a successful post-update confirmation from another affected AIO operator, and later superficially similar reports were directed to a separate issue.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Nextcloud administrator who can configure Authentik SAML, operate Nextcloud AIO, compare account types, test multiple deployments, and report version-specific behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and inquisitive; provides detailed configuration context, explains comparisons carefully, and asks for reasoning when maintainers reject an initial hypothesis.
